chunks: And from him, through his chain, from Al-Barqi, who said: Some of our companions narrated to us from 'Abbas ibn 'Amir Al-Qasbani, from Yaqtin, who said: Rabi' ibn Muhammad Al-Musli informed us:
Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) would say, when he entered the graveyard: Peace be upon the people of Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Al-Sadiq say when entering a graveyard?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the specific etiquette of the Ziyārah, where Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) greeted the deceased in graveyards with 'Peace be upon the people of Paradise,' affirming their status as inhabitants of Jannah. This practice underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory and honored status of the righteous dead, transforming the graveyard visit from a mere act of remembrance into a spiritual communion with the blessed. It reflects the broader theological concept that death is not an end but a transition to a higher state of existence for the believers.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 18. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Walīd narrated to me from someone whose name he mentioned, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ‘Abdillāh Al-Barqi, from some of our companions, from ‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir Al-Qasbāni, from Yaqťīn, from Rabī’ ibn Muḥammad Al-Musli, who said:
When Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) would enter a graveyard, he would say: Salām upon the people of Paradise.
